elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: New Section 31 covers only professional liability (E&O) and cyber/privacy liability; no commercial general liability per-occurrence limit appears anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No CGL aggregate limit is stated in Section 31 or elsewhere; the inserted covenant names only two coverage lines.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 31 requires 'professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000' \u2014 below the preferred USD 2,000,000 threshold.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The condition applies (TrueLink hosts the Web Site and transmits Client data through the Interface), but Section 31 sets cyber and privacy liability at only USD 2,000,000, not USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation obligation is inserted; the drafter expressly declined to volunteer it.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Section 31 contains no certificate-of-insurance delivery mechanic on request.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 31: 'TrueLink shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000'.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 31: '... and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000' \u2014 unconditional, so no data-category trigger limitation arises.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the inserted Section 31 states both required coverage lines in operative language with the exact amounts (E&O not less than USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy not less than USD 2,000,000), and both obligations run on TrueLink as the counterparty.

Preferred level is incomplete: no CGL per-occurrence or aggregate limits, E&O is USD 1,000,000 rather than USD 2,000,000, cyber is USD 2,000,000 rather than the USD 5,000,000 required where Vendor processes Customer Data, and there is no workers' compensation or certificates-on-request mechanic. To reach preferred, the drafter must raise E&O to USD 2,000,000, raise cyber/privacy to USD 5,000,000 for Customer Data processing, add CGL of USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate, add statutory workers' compensation, and add a certificate-on-request sentence.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single concise sentence limited to the two fallback coverage lines. The drafter correctly omitted the model-language extras (at-own-expense, term-plus-one-year survival tail, certificates) that would have been non-minimal at the fallback level, and no existing text was deleted or paraphrased.

Intent is preserved: Section 31 is appended after Section 30 (Force Majeure) without altering the retained force majeure language, creates no undefined term (TrueLink is a defined party), and leaves no dangling cross-reference or contradictory sentence; numbering continues cleanly from the existing Sections 13\u201330.
